text: The operation, the payload and the element names of the checked-fields read come from RWB-P5-E2025-CON and are never guessed; the treatment columns that carry the facts are named for the extracted codes (contract_amount, contract_date, mortgage_amount, registration_date, land_office, title_doc_no) with source_document_id, source_doc_version and source_table_version beside them, and the amounts and dates follow the numeric(18,2) and date conventions TSD S2 T3.1 already uses; the type-table version stamped on the row is the tableVersion of the reader's answer the facts were written from; and the masking of party_names is the hub's, applied to the value it returns, with this service storing no party name at all.
why: No source names the read across the boundary, no source gives the treatment a contract or mortgage column, no source says who stamps the type-table version, and the legacy note limits unmasked values to SY-CASEWF and SY-AGENT, which does not include this service; leaving any of them blank would make the story unbuildable, and inventing a business value would be worse.
read: Legacy RWB-E2-025 sections 11, 12 and 13; TSD S2 T3.1, T3.2 and T-A.1; FSD S2 A2.1.3.2; Architecture v5 slides 18 and 41; Template and Rules sections R5.5 DP-11 and R7.2 s12.
confirm: The rwb-document contract owner publishes the operation, the payload and the masking rule, and the rwb-treatment data owner approves the fact columns in the DDL.
impact: Medium: a change in the column set or the masking rule is a migration and one criterion, and no rewrite of the story.

text: This story is the secondary slice of legacy RWB-E2-025: the classification, the extraction, the review queue, the evaluation runner and the eleven legacy acceptance criteria AC1 to AC11 stay with RWB-P5-E2025-APP, and the two requirements of the plan's list that the legacy key puts out of scope (REQ-DCM-017 and REQ-DCM-018) are answered by the document hub and tested by no criterion here. The story writes eight criteria of its own.
why: The legacy key is split across rwb-document and two route services, and the same eleven criteria cannot be owned twice; the work package carries the key as Split (rework) with an empty acs list for this story.
read: Legacy RWB-E2-025 sections 1 to 19, its section 7 acceptance criteria and its section 19 out-of-scope list; Template and Rules section R7.2 s7; work package B-S2-06 story line for RWB-S2-E2025-APP.
applied_in: Story sections 1, 7 and 16; section 18 requirement rows; fragment acs and reqs
confirm: The P5 slice owner confirms that RWB-P5-E2025-APP carries the eleven legacy criteria word for word.
impact: Low: the split follows the ownership map and the work package.

text: No personal data is written, logged or put on an event by this story: the row, the log lines, the workflow input and any event payload carry the case ID, the treatment ID, the document ID and version, the type-table version, field codes, amounts and dates only. party_names is masked by the hub, is never mapped onto a column, and a property test fails the build if a party name reaches a row, a log line or a span attribute.
why: The guardrails of Template and Rules section R7.2 s17 and the legacy story's own guardrail forbid personal data in events, workflow inputs and logs, and the legacy authority note grants unmasked values to SY-CASEWF and SY-AGENT only, so this service must hold none.
read: Template and Rules section R7.2 s17; legacy RWB-E2-025 sections 12, 17 and BR7; Architecture v5 slides 22 and 42 notes (events carry IDs and facts, never personal data).
confirm: The privacy owner confirms the field set of the treatment read and of any payload the stage handles.
impact: Low: the payload is narrower than the sources allow.

text: The outbox, inbox and idempotency library, the parameters and reference-data client libraries, the workflow kit and the gateway-bff composite route are platform wave-0 and shared-library deliverables the service template already carries: they stand in no build row of this story, the metadata keeps Depends on (build) None and Contract dependencies RWB-P5-E2025-CON only, and the story builds against their fakes until they publish.
why: The pattern table adds five H rows and two C rows for DP-06, DP-07, DP-09, DP-10 and DP-19 while the work package's build list is empty and its only contract is the P5 one; every added row is a platform library or a contract the template or another service already publishes, and inventing H rows would change the plan's build sequence.
read: Template and Rules sections R5.4, R5.5 and R5.7; Architecture v5 slide 20 (every service from the service template and shared libraries); work package B-S2-06 story line for RWB-S2-E2025-APP.
confirm: The platform template owner confirms the library delivery ahead of wave 2.
impact: Medium: a late library delays the story, but no H row is invented in its build list.

text: The applied facts reach SCR-14 Treatment record and SCR-15 Settlement offer through the gateway-bff composite route, which composes the case read of rwb-case with the treatment read of this service, one hop each, read only; the route specification, the screen field list and the layout belong to RWB-PLT-N001-CON and the screen owners, and SCR-30 and SCR-31 show the hub's fields read only through the same route.
why: DP-19 replaces the monolith screen with a composite route, and no source publishes the route or the field list of the two treatment screens in this wave.
read: Template and Rules section R5.5 DP-19; Architecture v5 slide 20 (gateway-bff, one hop, 2 s, breaker per service); legacy RWB-E2-025 section 15 and the treatment screens of the sibling stories.
confirm: RWB-PLT-N001-CON publishes the SCR-14 and SCR-15 route and its merge order.
impact: Low: the read model is proved against the route fake and switched on with the screens.

text: This slice publishes no event and registers no Schedule, and both rows stay in the pattern list as prohibitions. DP-09 is used only through the outbox and inbox library for the idempotency table of rwb_treatment and the one write key of the apply: DocumentFieldsExtracted is produced by rwb-document and consumed by rwb-case only, and the two events of rwb-treatment, TreatmentApproved and TreatmentClosed, belong to the approval and plan stories. DP-10 registers nothing: the intake and retention Schedules are rwb-document's, and the stage clock the activity runs under is the parent workflow's.
why: Declaring a producer for an event that no source assigns would put an outbox row into a slice that owns no event, and declaring a Schedule would add a job no source places in this capability; carrying both as prohibitions keeps the pattern list intact and makes the reading visible.
read: Architecture v5 slides 18, 42, 43 and 44; Template and Rules section R5.5 DP-09 and DP-10; legacy RWB-E2-025 sections 12 and 13.
applied_in: Story sections 1, 3, 12.3, 12.4, 12.6, 13 and 17; fragment events_published and events_consumed
confirm: The event catalogue owner confirms that no event is assigned to the treatment-side document-fact fill.
impact: Low: no event and no Schedule means no catalogue change and no chart change.

text: The checked-fields read is consumed as one REST hop with a 2 s timeout and a breaker against the contract and its fake, as DP-11 and the work package give it, and not as a Temporal activity on queue rwb-document as the connection matrix of Architecture v5 slide 13 would have it; the payload, the state filter and the criteria are the same under either transport, so a later decision to move the call to Temporal changes the client and no criterion.
why: The architecture catalogue outranks the pattern table under the precedence of R3, but its P5 contract publishes no checked-field activity and its own slide 16 gives rwb-document no such activity either, so following the matrix would leave nothing to build against on Day 1 while the legacy interface and DP-11 both describe a call that returns a value within the request.
read: Architecture v5 slides 12, 13, 16 and 18; Template and Rules sections R3 and R5.5 DP-11; legacy RWB-E2-025 sections 9 and 12; work package B-S2-06 story line for RWB-S2-E2025-APP.
confirm: The architecture review confirms the call type of the S2 to P5 read before the contract is frozen.
impact: Medium: a move to Temporal rewrites CheckedFieldClient and its fake and no criterion of section 7.
